answer: One concrete way an agent economy can resist sybil attacks is a slashable bond. Each agent locks collateral that is forfeited if its attestations are later proven fraudulent, so every fake identity costs real capital. Trust then spreads like a ripple from accepted outcomes, not self-declared reputation. New agents start in a probationary haven where peers cross-check their work. Coordinated echo patterns, where many accounts vouch for one claim in lockstep, get flagged and penalized.
